newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Aug 8.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Friday:
* Citicorp said it would consolidate all advertising and marketing under one agency.
* Only seven months into this year and stock funds are having their second-best year ever.
* The FCC issued tough new rules aimed at cutting costs of phone calls overseas.
* American retailers in July enjoyed one of their strongest months of sales in two years.
* America Online posted a quarterly loss, although operating results were above analysts' expectations.
* Westinghouse's CBS unit promoted Leslie Moonves to president of CBS Television.
* Bonds slumped on Thursday, hurting stocks too, as the Dow Jones Industrials fell 71.31 points to 8188.
* DuPont said it would invest $1.7 billion in Pioneer Hi-Bred.
* An investor group led by the Thomas H. Lee companies agreed to buy Fisher Scientific for $1.4 billion.
* Kodak said the president of its struggling digital imaging business resigned.
* EDS reported declining earnings in the second quarter and said the poor results would continue all year.
* The NASD adopted rules that would make it harder for brokers from firms that violate securities laws to move onto other firms.
* GE agreed to sell six million PaineWebber shares back to the brokerage firm.
* Little progress was made in Thursday's contract talks between the Teamsters union and United Parcel Service.
